content: The term target cell is used in medicine to describe three distinct concepts, depending on the context: 1. In hematology, target cells refer to abnormal red blood cells that exhibit a characteristic bullseye appearance. These cells are also known as codocytes. 2. In endocrinology, target cells are those cells that are specifically affected by hormones. These cells possess receptors on their surface that allow hormones to bind to them. Hormones circulate through the bloodstream until they encounter a target cell with the appropriate receptor, enabling the hormone to exert its biological effect. 3. In immunology, target cells are the cells that directly receive the effector functions of T cells. These cells are specifically identified and targeted for cytotoxic destruction by T cells as part of the immune response.
